chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
A mourning gathering (ma'tam) is prepared for the family of the deceased for three days, from the day he died.

key_terms.مَأْتَمٌ: Mourning gathering or assembly held for the bereaved family

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed duration and nature of the mourning period (ma'tam) for the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the communal obligation of preparing a mourning gathering (ma'tam) for the bereaved family for three days, a practice deeply rooted in early Shia tradition as a support mechanism for the grieving household. It highlights the neighbor's duty to facilitate this period of communal solidarity, distinguishing the structured social response to death from the broader, longer mourning periods (iddah) observed by widows.
